All 264 source word occurrences are preserved in exact order and spelling: 224 eligible and 40 explicitly excluded nonspoken sound/action-description occurrences. Every eligible occurrence has a contextual Arabic explanation and four-option choice override. All row prompts, including excluded rows, are Arabic-only. 6 clips have no eligible occurrences. The five final translator-credit words are retained as intelligible written lexical text, explicitly not dialogue; Orhan and Cevher are personal names. No unresolved spelling hold was identified and no source spelling was corrected. Context distinguishes Sen var ya as discourse emphasis, sağ olasın as thanks with a wish, helal olsun as remission of a claim rather than praise, arama as a noun, fazla as degree of distance, Benim aracın as a colloquial omitted possessive rather than a typo, Baba in 1636 as the subject not vocative, at as a horse rather than an imperative, O kadar da as degree/emphasis, and şakşağındasın as a documented dialect door-knocker term in a contextual rebuke for dwelling on a minor issue. The police/military account is explained as dialogue rehearsal, not independently established fact; religious and appearance judgments are attributed to speakers.
